Hypervascular — enhance in the arterial phase
Localises small tumours and allows biopsy
Insulinoma is the commonest functional pNET and follows the 90% rule (90% benign, solitary, <2 cm, intrapancreatic) — confirm with a
supervised 72-hour fast and a negative sulfonylurea screen.
Gastrinoma causes Zollinger–Ellison syndrome (multiple / refractory ulcers with diarrhoea), often lies in the duodenal wall within the gastrinoma
triangle, and is frequently associated with MEN1 — always look for it.
Grade by Ki-67: G1 <3%, G2 3–20%, G3 >20%. A G3 NET is still well differentiated, whereas a neuroendocrine carcinoma (NEC) is poorly
differentiated and treated like small-cell (platinum + etoposide).
68Ga-DOTATATE PET-CT is the functional imaging of choice; chromogranin A is the general tumour marker, most useful in non-functional
A small (<2 cm), asymptomatic, non-functional G1 pNET can be safely surveilled rather than resected (ENETS).
In MEN1, hyperparathyroidism is the earliest and commonest feature and gastrinoma the commonest functional pNET — but MEN2 does not
Sources: WHO 2022 classification of neuroendocrine neoplasms (Ki-67 / mitotic grading; NET vs NEC) · ENETS / UKINETS guidance on gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms.
Functional imaging: 68Ga-DOTATATE PET-CT; general marker chromogranin A.
Trials: CLARINET (lanreotide) · NETTER-1 (177Lu-DOTATATE PRRT) · RADIANT-3 (everolimus) · sunitinib (Raymond et al., NEJM 2011). Completes the pancreatic series — 1 PDAC & Whipple
